subject: physics
question_text: A = i + j. What is the angle between the vector and the x-axis?

verification.note: Sri Chaitanya IPE Junior Fastrack (Rev. May 2024), VERY SHORT ANSWER 4 of Unit 4. The mark split is invented and needs a Telangana IPE teacher; no exam appearance years are printed for Unit 4, so appearances[] stays empty.

recall_prompt: Say the steps you would write for this answer, in order. You can speak in English, in Telugu, or in both.

page_header: Section A — Very Short Answer Question

steps.label: Set up tan α
lines: The x and y components are both 1.
If α is the angle with the x-axis,
steps.margin_note: Read the components straight off i + j: both are 1.
steps.why: The tangent of the direction angle is always the y component over the x component — here that ratio is 1.
common_mistakes: Using A_x / A_y, the ratio upside down.

accept: tan alpha is one by one
reject: the angle is forty five degrees

steps.memory_tip: tan α = y-component over x-component. Here both components are 1.

steps.label: The angle
steps.margin_note: One line. This is the fastest full-mark answer in the section.
steps.why: Equal components pull equally along x and y, so the vector points exactly midway — 45° from either axis.
steps.memory_tip: Equal pulls along x and y put the vector exactly midway: 45°.

insider_note: A one-line answer worth two marks. Write tan α = 1 above α = 45° — the working is half the credit.
